fieldNotes: This file describes the boards the WinUSB Demo Program can show. The program creates it from its built-in template when it is missing.
Edit it with any text editor, then select Reload in the program. Unknown fields, like this one, are ignored.
id: unique short name of the board. name: the descriptive name. productMatch: text (or a list of texts) found in the board's USB product name, e.g. 'GCBASIC WinUSB 18F4550'.
keepAlive: the LED that toggles on every keep-alive (request 255): name, io, port.

switches: up to four. name, io, port, usbCode (the request that reads them, 140 in the demonstration programs) replyByte (the byte of the reply, 0 = first) and onValue (the reading that shows the switch as on: 0 for a switch to 0V with a pull-up, 1 if left out).
switchPollSeconds: the poll period: Start Poll reads the switches every this many seconds until End Poll (0 or left out: no poll, only Read).
leds: name, io, colour (a .NET colour name such as Red, or #RRGGBB), port, usbCodeRead, usbCodeOn and usbCodeOff.
adc: name, io, port, channel (ANx or ANAx), range ('0-255', '0-1023' or '0-4095' for 12 bit), usbCode and replyByte. A range above 255 uses two bytes, low byte first.

usbControl: the name of a keep-alive, LED, switch or ADC channel in the firmware: USBCONTROLKEEPALIVE, USBCONTROLOUTPUT1 to 8, USBCONTROLINPUT1 to 4 (its replyByte is its number - 1), USBCONTROLADC1 to 4. headerFile: the firmware header Ctrl+G writes for the board, with these names, its pins and its request codes.
bodyText: the help text, one string per line.

boards.name: PICDEM FS USB Demo 18F4450 Board, 2004
bodyText: GCBASIC WinUSB application: no driver to install.
This application shows:
- The connection status. It finds the board when it is plugged in, and connects again after it is removed and plugged back in.
- Setting PIC outputs: use the Set boxes to turn the board's LEDs D1, D2 and D3 (RD0, RD1 and RD2: outputs 1, 2 and 3) on and off.

- Reading PIC inputs: select 'Read' to read the board's two switches (RB4 and RB5: inputs 1 and 2), or 'Start Poll' to read them every 10 seconds. A switch reads 0 when it is pressed (switches to 0V, pull-ups): its lamp is white.
- Reading the potentiometer: its value (0 to 1023, 10 bits, from RA0: AN0) is read with the switches, by 'Read' and 'Start Poll'. Turn it and read again.
- When it connects, it reads the state of the LEDs and the switches and shows it here.

- A keep-alive 10 seconds after the last USB transfer: LED D4 (RD3) toggles. The dots at the bottom right count the seconds to it. If it fails, the application closes the board and opens it again when it answers.
- No driver: the board's program (usb.h with USB_WCID) tells Windows 8.1 and later to load their own WinUSB driver.
The board: the PICDEM FS USB Demo Board with a PIC18F4550 and a 20 MHz crystal, WINUSB_18F4550_Demonstration.gcb.
Enjoy

boards.name: PIC18F14K50, 12 MHz crystal, one switch
bodyText: GCBASIC WinUSB application: no driver to install.
This application shows:
- The connection status. It finds the board when it is plugged in, and connects again after it is removed and plugged back in.
- Setting PIC outputs: use the Set State boxes to turn the red, yellow and green LEDs (I/O 2, 3 and 4) on and off.
- Reading PIC inputs: select 'Read' to read the switch (I/O 6). It reads 0 when it is pressed (a switch to 0V, pull-up).
- When it connects, it reads the state of the LEDs and shows it here.

- A keep-alive 10 seconds after the last USB transfer: the LED on I/O 1 toggles. The dots at the bottom right count the seconds to it. If it fails, the application closes the board and opens it again when it answers.
- No driver: the board's program (usb.h with USB_WCID) tells Windows 8.1 and later to load their own WinUSB driver.
The board: WINUSB_18F14K50_Demonstration.gcb. A 12 MHz crystal with the PLL.
Enjoy

boards.name: PIC18F Starter Kit 1 (18F46J50), LEDs on the OLED
bodyText: GCBASIC WinUSB application: no driver to install.
This application shows:
- The connection status. It finds the board when it is plugged in, and connects again after it is removed and plugged back in.

- Setting PIC outputs: use the Set boxes to turn the red, yellow and green LEDs (outputs 1, 2 and 3) on and off. The kit has no user LEDs: they are circles on its OLED, labelled RED, YEL and GRN, filled when on.

- Reading PIC inputs: select 'Read' to read the MENU button (RB0: input 2), or 'Start Poll' to read it every 10 seconds. It reads 0 when it is pressed: its lamp is white. The OLED also shows MENU pressed or released.
- When it connects, it reads the state of the LEDs and the MENU button and shows it here. The OLED shows 'USB: connected'.

- A keep-alive 10 seconds after the last USB transfer: the KA circle on the OLED toggles. The dots at the bottom right count the seconds to it. If it fails, the application closes the board and opens it again when it answers.
- No driver: the board's program (usb.h with USB_WCID) tells Windows 8.1 and later to load their own WinUSB driver.
The board: WINUSB_18F46J50_Demonstration.gcb, standalone (it replaces the kit's bootloader). It also builds for the 18F47J53.
Enjoy
